name: Branch orders and returns
description: One row per order. Twelve months of calendar 2025 across eight branches. Every number the system gives comes from one of the metrics below; the SQL template is filled only from the dimension and filter vocabulary in this file and from the period, never from free text.

metrics.name: orders
metrics.definition: Count of orders placed in the period, returned or not.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} COUNT(*) AS value_count, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: revenue
metrics.definition: Sum of the order value of every order placed in the period, before returns.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} CAST(SUM(order_value) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: returns
metrics.definition: Count of orders placed in the period that were later returned.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} SUM(CASE WHEN returned THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS value_count, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: returns_rate
metrics.definition: Returns divided by orders, as a percent: the share of orders placed in the period that were later returned.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} SUM(CASE WHEN returned THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS numerator, COUNT(*) AS denominator, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: returned_value
metrics.definition: Sum of the order value of the orders placed in the period that were later returned.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN returned THEN order_value ELSE 0 END) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: net_revenue
metrics.definition: Revenue minus returned value: the order value of the orders placed in the period that were not returned.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN returned THEN 0 ELSE order_value END) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: average_order_value
metrics.definition: Revenue divided by orders: the mean order value of the orders placed in the period.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} CAST(SUM(order_value) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS numerator, COUNT(*) AS denominator, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: largest_order
metrics.definition: The highest single order value among the orders placed in the period.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} CAST(MAX(order_value) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} {group_by}

metrics.name: mom_growth
metrics.definition: Revenue in the month minus revenue in the month before, divided by the month before, as a percent. The period must be one month, and January has no month before it in the data.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} month, CAST(SUM(order_value) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE month IN ({period_month}, {previous_month}) {filters} GROUP BY {dimensions} month ORDER BY month

metrics.name: qoq_growth
metrics.definition: Revenue in the quarter minus revenue in the quarter before, divided by the quarter before, as a percent. The period must be one quarter, and Q1 has no quarter before it in the data.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimensions} quarter, CAST(SUM(order_value) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE quarter IN ({period_quarter}, {previous_quarter}) {filters} GROUP BY {dimensions} quarter ORDER BY quarter

metrics.name: revenue_share
metrics.definition: A group's revenue divided by the revenue of every group in the period, as a percent. One dimension is required: the groups are its values.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimension} AS group_value, CAST(SUM(order_value) * 100 AS BIGINT) AS value_cents, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} GROUP BY {dimension}

metrics.name: orders_share
metrics.definition: A group's orders divided by the orders of every group in the period, as a percent. One dimension is required: the groups are its values.
metrics.sql: SELECT {dimension} AS group_value, COUNT(*) AS value_count, COUNT(*) AS rows_over FROM orders WHERE {scope} GROUP BY {dimension}
